- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.30) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward slightly.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3%.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after a peak), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast in subsequent days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early days (e.g., first 5–7 days); dampen initial forecast values.
- If sentiment history shows strong positive sentiment followed by negative sentiment, model may overreact; smooth transition in forecast.
- When sentiment is consistently low and price is stable, model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly to avoid missing downward trend.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment shifts in the last 3–5 days; ensure forecast adjusts to sentiment change within 1–2 days.
